items.title: Paginated reports in Power BI support outbound access protection (Preview)
items.excerpt: Paginated reports can combine data from Power BI semantic models and other data sources with external resources such as maps and images. Workspace admins can control which destinations the Power BI service can reach when it renders these reports. Paginated reports now support workspace outbound access protection (OAP). When a workspace admin enables OAP for a Fabric workspace, outbound connections from paginated reports are blocked by default. The workspace admin can then create OAP exception rules to allow the connection types and destinations that the reports in that workspace are supposed to access. Why control outbound access at the workspace level? OAP helps workspace admins reduce unintended outbound access when the Power BI service renders paginated reports. Report authors define the data and content their reports need, and workspace admins decide which connections to allow. Authors can keep designing print-ready operational, financial, and regulatory reports using approved connections. items.title: Workspace outbound access protection for Power BI semantic models and interactive reports (Generally Available)
items.excerpt: Workspace outbound access protection (OAP) is generally available for Power BI semantic models and interactive Power BI reports in Microsoft Fabric workspaces. With OAP, workspace admins can limit which data sources semantic models reach. They can also limit which semantic models in other workspaces interactive reports can query. These rules help reduce unintended outbound access and mitigate data exfiltration risks. Semantic model creators choose their data sources. Report authors choose their semantic models. Workspace admins decide which outbound connections they want to allow in their workspaces. You can have semantic models and reports in the same workspace if you don’t need strict governance controls. You can also place them in separate workspaces if you don’t want to give report authors direct access to the underlying data sources of the semantic models. Which workspace controls each connection An interactive report can always query a semantic model in its own local workspace. For a model in another workspace, however, the report workspace admin must add a Power BI Semantic Model exception to the report workspace’s OAP policy. items.title: OneLake: The unified foundation for data, context, governance, and AI
items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Most organizations' data is scattered across dozens of applications, clouds and services. Now that agents need to work across the entire business, organizations need to bring that data together in one place: one copy, open to every engine and team, without moving or duplicating it. Unified data gives agents reach, but to act with confidence they also need context: what the data means, how it connects to the business, who should see it and whether it can be trusted. OneLake is the single place for customers to unify their data estate. Shortcuts , mirroring , catalog federation and IQ Share bring multi-cloud, on-premises sources and databases and data platforms together into a single view of the data estate. The OneLake catalog provides a trusted place for organizations to easily explore, govern and secure data in OneLake. items.title: Bringing trusted Fabric IQ context to wherever people and agents work
items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Over the past year, AI has moved from answering questions to doing the work. As the 2026 Microsoft Work Trend Index shows, people are now handing entire tasks to agents and directing several at once. Those agents plan, decide, and act across systems, with less human review at every step. Fabric IQ helps turn your organization's business knowledge into an advantage for people and agents. As agents take on more responsibility, that knowledge matters more than which model they run on. Every organization can use the same frontier models. What sets yours apart is its context layer: the definitions, metrics, relationships, and rules that describe how your business actually works. When you connect that context with knowledge from across the organization, people and agents can uncover insights and take informed action that reflects how the business operates.
